title: Studying violin in New York and its bands
summary: In New York in 1923-24 he heard no real jazz bands, only string groups in Greenwich Village.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, here's something I think I would... I know you went to New York, you say, in the early 20s. You were playing mostly violin.
I was studying violin in New York, yeah. Had you been playing your cornet, of course, in... No, I hadn't been playing my cornet at that time. No, in a long time. I hadn't touched it.
When you heard the New York bands or if you'd heard any, was there much difference in the style or could you notice the difference between the New Outlings?
Oh, well, they didn't have any bands in those days, you know, around 1923 or 1924. They may have had a few.
Was anybody like Red Nichols or... No, no, no, uh-uh. The Darcys, any of those? No, uh-uh. Nobody like that that you heard at all?

No, no, no. If they were, I certainly didn't know anything about them. I hadn't bumped into them. The only thing I heard was... I lived in the village most of the time when I was there. Once in a while passing a nightclub and I'd hear a good hot fiddle player. Mostly string groups, you know. A violin and a piano and a drum. The same thing that they used in picture shows throughout the country, you know. Oh, yeah. Yeah, in groups like that. Violin, piano and a drum. And that was it for, I imagine, most of the little places that they had in the village.
Is that air conditioner getting too cool for you, Bill? No, no. Feels good, no.
So you don't have much of a recollection of any other real jazz in New York?
